messages:
Maya: Heads-up — a couple of UX nits I ran into while testing the model catalog compare flow.
Maya: 1) Performance badge meaning isn’t clear at a glance. color + icon combo is neat but people are asking what 'fast' vs 'balanced' maps to (latency target? cost?).
Maya: 2) When the filter rail collapses at small widths, the selected filters disappear visually — users think their selection cleared.
Jon: +1 on both. saw a user hesitate because the green badge made them assume low cost, but our defs are latency-first.
Jon: We should add a short tooltip copy and an accessible label. maybe pair color with explicit text in the tooltip: "Latency-focused — < 50ms P95 on typical infra" (tighter copy needed).
Sam: For the filter rail: we collapse to a compact icon list currently. the selected chips still exist but we don't show the count on the compact pill. Agree that feels like a loss of state.
Lina: Could we surface a tiny counter on the collapsed button? like "Filters (2)" but less visual weight.
Maya: Counter sounds good. Also for badges: what about making the tooltip show the metric + sample unit, and a link to a short explainer. e.g. tooltip body: ``Latency-first — P95 < 50ms on reference workload. Click to see test harness & dataset.``
Jon: Also need to consider contrast + icons for colorblind users. current amber/green combo fails some pairings at 12px.
Jon: Suggestion: add a subtle outline and an aria-label that reads the badge meaning: `aria-label="Performance: latency-first; P95 < 50ms"`.
Sam: Implementation note: tooltip component is shared. quick patch: add optional `meta` prop with `metricText` and `ariaLabel` so product teams can pass the strings without new components.
Sam: Example snippet we can use in the code review:

```
<Badge
  variant="performance"
  color="green"
  tooltipText="Latency-first — P95 < 50ms on reference workload"
  ariaLabel="Performance badge: latency-first; P95 under 50 milliseconds"
/>
```

Lina: Love that. For the filter collapse, we should also remember keyboard users — when the rail collapses the focus order changes and the next focus lands on the compare table, skipping filters.
Lina: Proposal: when collapsed, make the collapsed rail reachable by `Tab` and announce the selected count via `aria-live` when toggled.
Maya: Good call. @a11y-bot any quick automated checks we should add to PRs for color/contrast and missing aria-labels?
a11y-bot: Quick check suggestions: 1) Ensure contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for text/icons at small sizes 2) Each interactive badge must include aria-label 3) Collapsed filter toggle should have aria-expanded and an accessible name including selected count.
Jon: OK — next steps: Maya to draft tooltip microcopy + Lina to mock collapsed button with counter + Sam to add `meta` prop in badge component and wire ariaLabel.
Maya: I'll drop a Figma version in ~30m: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/model-catalog-badges (WIP)
Sam: I'll pick this up after stand. will aim for a small PR with the prop + unit tests.
Lina: I'll prototype the collapsed state and keyboard flow, will ping @Jon for visual QA.
Maya: Thanks — let's aim to ship this as a small improvement (no feature flag) but hold for a quick design/dev review before merge.
Jon: :thumbsup:
Maya: Filing a short follow-up note in the design board so PMs and support can update docs if we change meanings.
Maya: cc @all — any other thoughts?
